question: Which established review practices (reporting, protocol, question framing, evidence grading, rapid and software engineering adaptations) can ESOI adopt for every knowledge search, and where does it need its own part?
decision: adopt, adapt or build the research standard
method: Web search against criteria fixed before the first query; titles and result summaries screened, nothing opened in full.
criteria: include: the current canonical statement or guideline of a review practice with a citable identifier; exclude: teaching handouts and glossaries as the source of a claim
queries: web | PRISMA 2020 statement BMJ 2021 | 2026-11-10 | 10; web | Cochrane Handbook current version and rapid reviews | 2026-11-10 | 10; web | Kitchenham Charters SLR guidelines software engineering protocol | 2026-11-10 | 10; web | GRADE Guyatt 2008 and PRISMA-S | 2026-11-10 | 10; web | PRISMA-S extension Rethlefsen 2021 | 2026-11-10 | 10; web | PICO Richardson 1995 | 2026-11-10 | 10; web | PRISMA-P 2015 and PROSPERO | 2026-11-10 | 10; web | grey literature multivocal reviews software engineering | 2026-11-10 | 10
screened_out: 62 mirror or repository copy of a kept source;6 teaching handout or glossary;4 translated or unrelated page
synthesis_known: A protocol before searching, counted screening, a reporting checklist for the search and a certainty grade per finding are settled practice in medicine, carried into software engineering by Kitchenham and Charters and by Garousi and colleagues.
synthesis_contested: How little a rapid review may omit before it misleads (Cochrane's rapid guidance gives 24 recommendations and no single threshold); whether PICO fits exploratory questions.
synthesis_unknown: How well an AI-run review matches a human one; no source found measures it.
limitations: Every item read through search-result summaries, not opened in full; author lists not checked; only the web was searched, no paper index.
decisions: Kitchenham and Charters protocol-first plan: adopt: the software engineering adaptation of the medical method;PRISMA 2020: adapt: screening counts and limitations;PRISMA-S: adapt: queries with dates and hits;PRISMA-P: adapt: method fixed and dated before the work;PICO: adapt: four engineering slots;Cochrane rapid review guidance: adapt: three sizes by the weight of the decision;Garousi grey literature: adapt: vendor documentation as a source of the lowest grade;GRADE: build-on: the repository's own A to D grade rather than four certainty levels
